hypothesis: Replacing the per-byte inString handling in LineIndex.build (src/indexer/lineIndex.ts L247-251) with a dedicated string-skip inner loop whose body is a 4x-unrolled fast reject (skip while buf[i..i+3] are all > 0x5c), with backslash pairs consumed inline and `escaped` carried across chunk boundaries, will raise the primary speedup from 0.898 to ~1.40-1.59, because ~75% of fixture bytes are string bytes > 0x5c that currently each pay a full outer-loop iteration plus three state checks. This is the only change: the switch cases, checkpoint modulo, record pushes, for-await loop, Buffer.from conversion and EOF handling are untouched.

steps.change: Inside the `for await (const raw of handle)` body, replace ONLY the per-chunk byte loop, i.e. lines 245-294 from `for (let i = 0; i < n; i++) {` through its matching closing `}` (the line right before `totalBytes += n;`). Lines 241-244 (`for await`, `const buf = ...`, `const n = buf.length;`, `const chunkBase = totalBytes;`) and everything from `totalBytes += n;` (L295) to the end of build stay byte-for-byte identical. Do not add module-level constants, helper functions, DataView, tables, new state variables, or any nextCp / lazy-record / extraction change.

Verification (no file edits): run the project's typecheck/build and the existing test suite as defined in package.json; all must pass. Then run a differential check of the new LineIndex.build against the sealed original bytewise reference on the sealed edge fixtures plus: escaped quote and escaped backslash split at every byte position (1-byte chunk splits), trailing backslash at EOF, raw newline inside a string, string left open at EOF (with and without trailing newline), unbalanced brackets, empty/blank leading lines, unicode, splits of 1/2/7/64/1000 bytes, checkpointInterval 1/3/1024, async-iterable, sync-iterable and string-chunk inputs; compare checkpoints, totalBytes, totalLines, multiline flag, recordEndLines, recordEndOffsets and endsWithNewline for exact equality. Finally run node scripts/benchmark-index-build.mjs (sealed, unmodified) at least 3 times and report the median primary speedup.

expected_outcome.estimated_impact: +55-75% (primary ~1.40-1.59 vs baseline 0.898); does not by itself reach the 1.8 target
expected_outcome.rationale: 75% of the 16 MB fixture's bytes are string padding ('x'/'y'/'z', all > 0x5c). The current code runs a full outer iteration per string byte (load, inString test, escaped test, two compares, continue). The tight loop removes the outer-loop overhead and the 4x unroll checks four bytes per bounds check with a single compare each. Round-2 scratch measured this exact candidate (e3 tight+rej4) at 1.374/1.383/1.530/1.590/1.499 across five processes, with the scratch mirror of current code at 0.79-0.91 and the real build at 0.78-0.92 in the same processes, so ratios transfer ~1:1. Noise is ~±0.05-0.08, far below the expected delta, so the result is decisively testable.

history_reference.builds_on: round_1_planner_a (tight string-skip loop, rejected only for bundling nextCp under H001) and research brief round_2 idea 1 (tight+rej4, highest-confidence single change); round_1 lesson that gains must come from the inner string loop, not from restructuring.
history_reference.avoids: Bundling of any second change (nextCp counter, lazy record storage, hasFirst guard, outer non-structural skip, SWAR/DataView) per H001 and round-1 critic rejections; ScanState/kernel extraction (round_1_planner_b, 0.897 neutral); Uint8Array class table in strings (slower, 1.151); 8x unroll (1.25, worse than 4x); Buffer#indexOf skipping (slower on short strings, wrong for raw newlines in strings).
